Simulated weekly bird song counts with hierarchically correlated AR(1) trends

Source: R/birdsong.R
birdsong.Rd

A multivariate count time series for four bird species observed weekly across 80 weeks. Each species has its own AR(1) latent trend; the four series are coupled through a contemporaneous innovation correlation matrix. Two species (warbler, thrush) rise together; two (wren, finch) move opposite to them. A shared cyclic seasonal smooth is added on week-within-year.

Usage

birdsong

Format

A data.frame with 320 rows and the following fields:

series

factor identifying the species (warbler, thrush, wren, finch); duplicated as species for readability.

time

integer week index from 1 to 80.

y

integer weekly count (Poisson sampled); duplicated as count.

species

factor, alias of series.

week

integer week index, alias of time.

week_in_year

integer week within the annual cycle (1..52), used for the shared seasonal smooth.

count

integer weekly count, alias of y.

Details

An independent-AR fit (trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1)) treats the four trajectories as unrelated. trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1, cor = TRUE) recovers the cross-species correlation that couples them.

True generative components:

  • Species random intercepts (centred) on the log scale.

  • Shared cyclic seasonal smooth (mgcv bs = "cc") on week-within-year.

  • Hierarchically correlated AR(1) trends with phi = 0.7 and innovation standard deviation 0.35. The 4 x 4 innovation correlation matrix sets (warbler, thrush) against (wren, finch).

See also

AR() for the trend, residual_cor() to extract the fitted correlations between species, mvgam_data() to check the data.

Examples

data(birdsong)
mvgam_data(birdsong, family = poisson())
#> ✔ Data check passed for family 'poisson (link = log)'.
#> • series: 4 levels
#> • time:   1 to 80
#> • n obs:  320 (0 NA)


# \dontrun{
# A model with the structure the data were simulated from
mod <- mvgam(
  formula = y ~ s(week_in_year, bs = "cc", k = 8) +
                s(species, bs = "re"),
  trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1, cor = TRUE),
  data = birdsong,
  family = poisson(),
  chains = 2, silent = 2
)
summary(mod)
#>  Family: poisson 
#>   Links: mu = log 
#> Formula: y ~ s(week_in_year, bs = "cc", k = 8) + s(species, bs = "re") 
#>    Data: birdsong (Number of observations: 320)
